newsitem.title: USA: CME LUMBER FUTURES FALL LATE ON CASH WEAKNESS.
newsitem.headline: CME LUMBER FUTURES FALL LATE ON CASH WEAKNESS.

text.p: Despite the official weekly quote that pointed to higher prices, the most recent trend in cash was lower and CME lumber futures fell late along with declining spruce prices, traders said.
Lumber closed $7.70 to $1.90 per tbf lower with September off most at $342.80 after trading up to $353.00 early and November ended off $4.70 at $340.80 per tbf.

Early short covering gave way to increased pressure from a downturn in the cash market. Selling by RBH then touched off some sell stops and September fell for a $8.90 loss in the closing range, traders said.
Random Lengths quoted cash spruce at $355, up $3 from Friday and $11 over last week. However, they reported that sales have slowed at the mill level.
Later reports put cash down $5 to $10 at $345 per tbf. Retailers were not willing to pay the higher prices, especially ahead of the seasonal slowdown in demand, cash sources said.
